notes: adapter_mode=mock: token counts are synthetic and deterministic; treat cost figures as a model of spend, not observed spend.
Ablation baseline auto-selected: 'baseline' (fewest billable tokens per task).
Costs are re-derived from the price book over recorded token counts, so the report can be restated with a different price book without re-running.

pareto.explanation: 8 of the candidates are non-dominated: mock-small / baseline -> mock-small / cot -> mock-small / fewshot-compress -> gpt-4o-mini / baseline -> deepseek-chat / baseline -> deepseek-reasoner / baseline -> deepseek-reasoner / cot -> deepseek-reasoner / fewshot-compress. Cheapest is mock-small / baseline; the best value is mock-small / cot (highest quality per dollar); the best quality is deepseek-reasoner / fewshot-compress. Knee point (farthest from the line joining the cost/quality extremes) is deepseek-chat / baseline at $0.000676/task and quality 0.763 — the last point where extra spend still buys a proportionate amount of quality. Across the frontier, quality rises at 138.688 points per USD ($0.007210 per quality point). Baseline for the ablation table is deepseek-reasoner / baseline.

retry.explanation: Retries burned $0.073400 of $1.955702 total spend (3.75% of the bill, 3.52% of billable tokens) — that share is pure waste: it bought no additional graded output. Worst offender is deepseek-reasoner / baseline: $0.026314 of retry spend (5.74% of that group's cost) from 6/150 retried cells, dominated by 'rate_limit' errors. 80/2250 cells needed a retry, 82 extra attempt(s) in total.

cache.explanation: Caching already saved $0.073436 (3.62% of the $2.029138 no-cache bill) at the observed token-weighted hit rate of 48.9% across 2250 cell(s). Pushing every prompt to a 100% hit rate would take the bill to $1.880936, a further $0.074766 (3.82%) below the observed $1.955702. Marginal value: $0.014820 saved per +10 percentage points of cache hit rate.

experiment.name: frontier-flagship
experiment.description: 5 models x 3 prompt strategies over the 50-task coding benchmark, 3 repeats. Measures quality-per-dollar and attributes token deltas to individual prompt knobs (system length, few-shot count, chain-of-thought, tool compression).

strategies.description: Control arm: short system prompt, no few-shot examples, no reasoning instruction, tool output passed through verbatim. The cheapest defensible prompt, and the reference point for every delta in the report.

baseline plus a chain-of-thought instruction. Same system prompt, same task text; only the reasoning directive (and the longer answers it provokes) differs, so this arm prices "think before you answer".

baseline plus 3 category-matched few-shot exemplars and tool-output compression. Two opposing cost forces in one arm: exemplars add input tokens, compression removes ~1,200 of them on the six tool-use tasks. The report's strategy-delta table separates the two effects.
